source_review.notes: Reviewed ten sources covering information hiding, structured design, object-oriented coupling metrics, dependency direction, modularity, architecture-organization mirroring, dependency models, graph theory, software architecture, and team interactions. Crossref metadata confirmed all five cited article and proceedings DOIs. Publisher and author-maintained records confirmed the cited Clean Architecture edition and the Team Topologies second edition, including its 23 September 2025 publication date. Book identities and editions were checked without claiming that a catalog page proves every interpretation in the chapter; the only materially current bibliographic claim is dated and bound to the retrieval date.

evidence: Reviewed the typed directed multigraph, afferent and efferent coupling, instability, reachability, propagation-cost, Jaccard, and edge-weight definitions.
Confirmed every denominator and domain condition is stated, including undefined instability for an isolated node and propagation cost only for more than one node.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Consumer-to-provider edge orientation is declared and used consistently after correcting the SCC condensation example.

evidence: Recomputed the executable graph as billing Ca=1 Ce=1 I=0.50, ledger Ca=1 Ce=0 I=0.00, and web Ca=0 Ce=2 I=1.00.
Recomputed the four-node chain as six reachable nonself ordered pairs out of twelve, giving propagation cost 0.5.
Recomputed Exercise 2 as A=(0,2,1), B=(1,1,0.5), C=(2,1,1/3), D=(1,0,0), with six reachable pairs and propagation cost 0.5.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Ratios are structural descriptors for declared graphs and are never interpreted as probabilities or universal quality scores.

evidence: Verified instability remains in [0,1] whenever Ca and Ce are nonnegative and their sum is positive.
Verified the propagation-cost numerator cannot exceed n(n-1) when reachability is Boolean and self pairs are excluded.
Verified SCC contraction yields an acyclic condensation graph: any cycle among contracted nodes would imply those nodes belong to one larger SCC.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The symbolic checks establish formula bounds and graph properties, not architectural desirability.

evidence: Reviewed isolated nodes, one-node and coarse-grained graphs, parallel typed edges, cycles, hubs, stable high fan-in, and reversed edge orientation.
Reviewed reflection, generated code, plugins, forwarding facades, shared libraries, brokers, schemas, identity, clocks, and control planes as hidden-dependency cases.
Reviewed node merging, renaming, edge reclassification, excluded runtime paths, bulk commits, and employee-ranking misuse as adversarial or gaming cases.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Critical common causes and physical, safety, privacy, supplier, and regulatory coupling remain outside the assurance supplied by graph counts alone.

evidence: Traced every metric to graph type, node granularity, direction, extractor, scope, revision, and exclusions.
Confirmed direct and transitive dependence, code and runtime graphs, correlation and causation, and undefined and zero values remain distinct.
Confirmed no purported improvement passes solely by hiding edges while change, deployment, authority, or failure propagation worsens.
invariant_checking.notes: Outcome evidence and stakeholder consequences guard the structural measurements.

evidence: Reviewed the executable degree calculation against the literal graph and exact output.
Reviewed the SCC-condensation argument and corrected its external edge to checkout -> SCC under the chapter's consumer-to-provider convention.
Reviewed the reachability calculations and the counterexamples showing equal propagation cost does not establish appropriate dependency direction.
proof_review.notes: The chapter makes bounded deductions from declared graphs and does not offer a theorem that a metric proves modularity, safety, resilience, or team quality.

evidence: Audited uses of prove, establish, independent, causal, decoupled, stable, failure, and quality for explicit qualifications.
Confirmed graph possibility, observed runtime behavior, design inference, and organizational hypothesis are not conflated.
Confirmed the chapter identifies qualitative review and experiments needed beyond each structural measure.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The executable example explicitly limits its evidence to the supplied direct import graph.

evidence: Executed snippet structural-coupling with the repository verifier under the recorded Python 3 toolchain.
Observed exit status 0, exact three-line stdout for billing, ledger, and web, and empty stderr.
The snippet report records source, command, toolchain, actual and expected output, status, and environmental limitations.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution validates only the literal graph arithmetic; it does not validate dependency extraction from a production system or infer runtime, data, authority, deployment, or organizational coupling.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed typed graph construction, static extraction, degree, instability, SCCs, reachability, runtime, data, authority, deployment, change, organizational and failure coupling, comparison normalization, contextual thresholds, gaming resistance, interventions, and evidence limits for architectural coherence.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed executable extraction boundaries, mixed-version deployment, messaging backlog, shared control planes, hidden common causes, co-change confounders, incident propagation, graph versioning, and fitness-function enforcement. The advice requires raw evidence, fixtures, observations, failure tests, ownership, and explicit residual risk. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified graduate-depth formal and production reasoning, eighteen distinct misconceptions, one reproducible code example, ten nonduplicative worked examples with explicit conclusions, and five progressive exercises with complete answers ending in an unfamiliar international cold-chain transfer problem.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed. Source checks, graph derivations, one local Python execution, and conceptual review do not validate a real repository extractor, deployed topology, organizational design, failure independence, safety case, security posture, privacy compliance, or architecture correctness.
